about: One row per kind of lawmaking body (engine map line 28, E3: one bill engine, the level a row). The bill and budget engine (src/core2/modules/legislature.ts) reads a body's level, the legislature its chambers belong to, the chamber a bill or budget starts in, the words for the body, whose law its bills make (`law`: the nation's, the state's, the county's, the township's or the place's), a member's term where the chamber fixes it (`termYears`), the tie-breaking rule the chamber reads from data/research/elections/tie-rules-2026.json (`tieBreaker`), and who holds the veto, from these rows instead of branching on the office kind. `kindPrefix` matches an office kind (us-house also covers the delegate and at-large rows). A body with no `legislature` is a one-chamber body. `chamberId` is the nation's own id for a federal chamber, which has one office row per state, and `jurisdiction` the nation's key. Structure is law (U.S. Const. art. I; state constitutions; county and municipal codes); each row cites it.

bodies.source: U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 1, 2 and 7: Congress is a House and a Senate; Representatives serve two years; revenue bills originate in the House.
U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 1 and 3: Senators serve six years; the Vice President breaks a tie (sec. 3, cl. 4).
Each state constitution's legislative article: the lower chamber (house, assembly or house of delegates).
Each state constitution's legislative article: the senate; where the constitution gives the lieutenant governor the tie-breaking vote, data/research/elections/tie-rules-2026.json names it.
Neb. Const. art. III, sec. 1: one chamber; the one legislature- row its state has.
State county codes: the county's governing board adopts its budget and its ordinances are county law (src/core2/gov-rules/county-governing-body-rules.ts).
Municipal charters and codes: the council is the municipal legislative body (src/core2/data/offices/body-names.json).
State township codes: where the town's own government is its township, the township board is its legislative body and its ordinances bind the township.

vetoHolder.source: U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 7 (the president's veto); state constitutions (the governor's); county and municipal charters (the county executive's and the mayor's, where the office exists). The holder's office sits at the government's own level.
